questions.explanation:
Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical policy design and enforcement in a real multi-tenant CNF gateway, focusing on OSS Gatekeeper usage, per-namespace configuration, and testability.

Key Concepts

- Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplate and Constraint
- Rego policy referencing namespace ConfigMap values
- Per-tenant overrides via Namespace annotations/config
- Lightweight tests to verify enforcement
- Minimal YAML scaffolding for quick rollout checks

Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate: defines RateLimitTemplate for K8sRateLimit
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8sratelimittemplate
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sRateLimit
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8sratelimit
      # Pseudocode: reads per-namespace cnf.rate-limit and enforces a per-minute cap
      defaultRate := 100
      rateLimitPerMin := data.rateLimitPerMin
      # implementation would map namespace to rate and count requests
      # returns deny if burst exceeds rate
```

```yaml
# Constraint: per-tenant rate limit value
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sRateLimit
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-rate-limit
spec:
  match:
    kinds:
    - apiGroups: [""]
      kinds: ["Namespace"]
  parameters:
    rateLimitPerMin: 200
    targetPath: "/gateway"
```

```yaml
# Namespace manifest overriding default rate for tenant-a
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
  annotations:
    cnf.rate-limit: "200"  # override default 100/min
```

```yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:

    command: ["sh", "-c", "for i in {1..150}; do curl -s http://gateway-service/gateway || true; done"]
```

## Why This Is Asked

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical design for per-tenant feature gating in CNF gateways, including secure identity, dynamic policy delivery, and runtime enforcement. It emphasizes end-to-end testability and real-world trade-offs between performance and isolation.

## Key Concepts

- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation
- in-memory enforcement with cache invalidation
- SPIFFE/SVID-based mutual TLS for control plane–sidecar trust
- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml
# Sample policy (per-tenant)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  features:
    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---

spec:
  replicas: 1

    matchLabels:

          volumeMounts:

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to architect cross-cluster, tenant-isolated config rollouts with dynamic proxy configuration.

## Key Concepts
- Envoy xDS dynamic configuration and Aggregated Discovery Service (ADS)
- Kubernetes CRD-based policy model per tenant with isolation
- Canary traffic shaping with weight and time-based rollout window
- Multi-cluster consistency and safe rollback mechanisms
- Observability hooks for validation during rollout phases

## Code Example
```yaml
# (a) Tenant Routing Policy with Canary Weight and Rollout Window
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: TenantRoutePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-api-v2
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  tenant: tenant-a
  targetCluster: cluster-west
  route:
    path: /api/v2
    backendRefs:
      - name: gateway-service
        port: 8080
  canary:
    weight: 0  # Start at 0%
    rolloutDuration: 30m
    stepWeight: 10  # Increment by 10% each step
    stepInterval: 5m
  rollback:
    enabled: true
    failureThreshold: 5  # Rollback if 5 consecutive errors exceed threshold
    errorRateThreshold: 0.05  # 5% error rate triggers rollback
  healthCheck:
    endpoint: /healthz
    interval: 30s
    timeout: 10s
---
# (b) Sidecar Config to Watch Policy and Push Updates
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: envoy-gateway-sidecar
  namespace: gateway-system
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: xds-controller
          image: cnf/xds-controller:latest
          args:
            - --policy-namespace=tenant-a
            - --xds-address=$(POD_IP):18000
            - --sync-interval=10s
          env:
            - name: POD_IP
              valueFrom:
                fieldRef:
                  fieldPath: status.podIP
          volumeMounts:
            - name: policy-config
              mountPath: /etc/policy
              readOnly: true
        - name: envoy
          image: envoyproxy/envoy:latest
          args:
            - --config-path /etc/envoy/envoy.yaml
            - --service-cluster gateway
          volumeMounts:
            - name: envoy-config
              mountPath: /etc/envoy
      volumes:
        - name: policy-config
          configMap:
            name: tenant-policies
        - name: envoy-config
          emptyDir: {}
---
# (c) One-Namespace Test Manifest for Canary Rollout and Rollback
apiVersion: cnf.example/v1
kind: CanaryRolloutTest
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-canary-test
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  policyRef:
    name: tenant-a-api-v2
  testStages:
    - stage: baseline
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 0
      checks:
        - type: metrics
          metric: requests_total{path="/api/v2"}
          condition: equals 0
    - stage: canary_10pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 10
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/health
          expectSuccessRate: 0.95
        - type: metrics
          metric: envoy_cluster_upstream_rq_xx{cluster="backend-v2"}
          condition: exists
    - stage: canary_50pct
      duration: 10m
      expectedWeight: 50
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/users
          expectSuccessRate: 0.99
    - stage: full_rollout
      duration: 5m
      expectedWeight: 100
      checks:
        - type: http
          url: http://gateway.tenanta.svc/api/v2/**
          expectSuccessRate: 0.999
  rollbackTest:
    enabled: true
    triggerFailureAt: canary_50pct
    expectedBehavior: weight_reverts_to_0_within_2m
```

## Why This Is Asked
Explores runtime attestation, cross-region provenance, and tenant-visible evidence beyond static gate checks.

## Key Concepts
- Runtime attestation and sidecars
- Central provenance store and immutability
- SBOM integrity and Cosign signatures
- Per-tenant evidence badges and audit trails

## Code Example
```yaml
# Verifier Deployment (simplified)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: cnf-verifier
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: verifier
        image: myregistry/provenance-verifier:latest
        env:
        - name: PROVENANCE_URL
          value: https://provenance.example/tenants/tenant-a
        - name: ALLOWLIST
          valueFrom:
            configMapKeyRef:
              name: tenant-a-config
              key: allowlist
        securityContext:
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
      imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
```

## Code Example

```yaml
# ConstraintTemplate (yaml)
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simageprovenance
spec:
  crd:
    spec:
      names:
        kind: K8sImageProvenance
  targets:
  - target: admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh
    rego: |
      package k8simageprovenance
      violation[{"msg": msg}] {
        input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
        some c in input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers
        not startswith(c.image, "ghcr.io/")
        msg := "image provenance missing or not tenant-approved"
      }
```

```yaml
# Constraint (yaml)
apiVersion: constraints.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: K8sImageProvenance
metadata:
  name: per-tenant-provenance
spec:
  enforcementAction: deny
  parameters:
    allowedTenant: "tenant-a"
```

```yaml
# Compliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
```

```yaml
# Noncompliant Deployment (yaml)
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-gateway-bad
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: gateway
        image: unsigned/gateway:latest
```

```bash
# Kubectl steps (one namespace first)
kubectl create ns tenant-a
# 1) Register constraint template and constraint
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_template.yaml
kubectl apply -f k8simageprovenance_constraint.yaml
# 2) Sign and SBOM-attach a valid image (tenant-a key)
cosign sign --key cosign-tenant-a.key ghcr.io/tenant-a/gateway:v1.0.0
# 3) Deploy compliant manifest
kubectl apply -f compliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 4) Deploy noncompliant manifest (unsigned)
kubectl apply -f noncompliant-deploy.yaml -n tenant-a
# 5) Check Gatekeeper denials and logs
kubectl get events -n tenant-a
kubectl describe deployment tenant-a-gateway-bad -n tenant-a
```
